title: Provably Protecting Fine-Tuned LLMs from Training Data Extraction while Preserving Utility
claim: Our smoothing-based algorithm keeps per-token deviation bounds orders of magnitude tighter than prior methods, with modest cost as parameters vary.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side, line plot left, log-scale overlaid histogram right
description: Two matplotlib-style plots side by side, labeled (a) and (b) below. Panel (a) is a line chart of B against log2(m), running from 0 to about 13. It has three downward-sloping curves for C=50% (blue), C=90% (orange) and C=99% (green). Higher C gives a higher curve, and all three converge toward small values as m grows. Panel (b) shows overlaid translucent histograms of k_x on a log-scale y-axis from 10^0 to 10^4. CP-Δ (blue) has a wide spread out to about 18. CP-Δ_r (orange) and SCP-Δ_r (green) are tight spikes near 0 to 1, with green the most concentrated. The eye goes first to the wide blue tail contrasted with the narrow green and orange spikes.
caption: Expected SpaRPS and $k_x$ evaluated using the MathAbstracts dataset (See [ref]). (a) Expected SpaRPS $B$ as a function of $\log_2(m)$ for different $C$ values. (b) $k_x$ bounds log-scale histograms for different CP style algorithms.
abstract: Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) on sensitive datasets raises privacy concerns, as training data extraction (TDE) attacks can expose highly confidential information. Existing defenses against such attacks either lack formal privacy guarantees or incur substantial utility degradation. We observe that fine-tuning induces widespread probability shifts, yet preserving only a small subset of influential token-level deviations is sufficient; the remaining shifts can be aggressively smoothed with minimal impact on utility. Motivated by this insight, we propose SCP-$Î_r$, a Near Access Freeness (NAF)-based algorithm that operates on relative probabilities and explicitly smooths low-impact tokens using a base model. SCP-$Î_r$ achieves orders-of-magnitude better theoretical bounds than existing NAF based methods and provides strong empirical protection against TDE attacks with minimal performance loss.
